message.content: {"pharmakon_274e":{"rendering":"medicine","gloss":"medicine, a healing substance","category":"remedy/medicine","note":"Taylor's text reads 'For this invention is the medicine of memory and wiſdom.' The Greek's agent/passive 'was found' becomes 'invention is'. The long Neoplatonic commentary interrupts the passage but does not change the word."},"mneme_274e":{"rendering":"memory","gloss":"memory","note":"Earlier in the speech, 'increaſe their powers of memory' renders mnemonikoteros; here the genitive is 'of memory'."},"sophia_274e":{"rendering":"wiſdom","gloss":"wisdom (long-s printing)","note":"Spelled with a long s in the source text."},"pharmakon_275a":{"rendering":"medicine","gloss":"medicine, a healing substance","category":"remedy/medicine","note":"Same word as at 274e: 'you have not diſcovered the medicine of memory, but of admonition.' The genitive 'of' is repeated only once for the second noun."},"mneme_275a":{"rendering":"memory","gloss":"memory","note":"Same word as at 274e. Earlier in Thamus's speech, 'recollection' is used for mnemes ameletesia ('negligence of recollection'), so the vocabulary for memory/recollection shifts in the neighbouring sentence."},"hypomnesis_275a":{"rendering":"admonition","gloss":"admonition, warning/reminding","note":"Taylor uses 'admonition' (a warning or chiding) rather than 'reminding' or 'reminder'. This loses the verbal link to memory (hypo-mnesis) that 'recollection' elsewhere in the passage would have kept, and adds a hortatory sense."},"sophia_275a":{"rendering":"an opinion of wiſdom","gloss":"an opinion of wisdom (long-s printing)","note":"Taylor renders doxa as 'opinion' and ties it to wisdom. 'not truth' renders ouk aletheian. 'Opinion' is neutral and lacks the sense of mere seeming or reputation."},"doxosophoi_275b":{"rendering":"poſſeſſing an opinion of wiſdom","gloss":"possessing an opinion of wisdom (long-s printing)","note":"The compound doxosophoi is not given as a single word but unpacked into a participial phrase, followed by 'inſtead Of wiſdom itſelf' for anti sophon. The 'seeming-wise' coinage is lost, and it repeats the same phrase as 'an opinion of wiſdom' above."},"argument":"Taylor keeps one word, 'medicine', for both occurrences of pharmakon, so Thamus does turn Theuth's own word against him: the same remedy is merely re-aimed from memory to 'admonition'. The healing sense stays throughout, and the poison/drug ambivalence is not available. Because hypomnesis becomes 'admonition' and doxosophoi becomes a periphrasis, the memory/reminding contrast and the 'wise-seeming' pun are weakened."}
